super_series_anchor_status: REPO-BASED, VERIFIED IN LIVE CODE (session-14): bot/src/index.js runSuperQueueSweep (line ~1648) discovers anchors by scanning listJobIds + probing each jobs/<id>/super-plan.json via isSuperSeriesAnchor (line ~1673: anchor iff super-plan.json has plan.parts array and spawned.length < total_parts). superQueueTick takes preloaded options and NEVER reads/writes the D1 super_series_anchor flag. The ONE remaining D1 write of that flag is handleSuperPlanUploadMessage line 1631 (setTaskOptions { super_series_anchor: true }) — a vestigial no-op that nothing reads anymore. D1's remaining legitimate roles: task_labels (per-chat A/B/C labels), task_options (mode/source_kind bookkeeping + super_halted_notified_part), clone_jobs (Worker-side clone resume), awaiting_input, announced markers. For the Dashboard ALL of these become client-side (localStorage) or repo-based: the Dashboard IS the operator's own client, so per-chat label state becomes localStorage, and clone-creation resume becomes client-side polling (the Dashboard browser tab does what the bot cron did). After task-12 deletes the Worker, the sweep must move to a GitHub-native cron (a scheduled workflow) — noted as a task-12 prerequisite.
